Issues.Title: QuestionAnsweringTrainer cannot produce answers with characters above U+00FF (answer is decoded one byte per character)
Issues.Body:
### Description

`QuestionAnsweringTrainer` (`Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp`, `Roberta/QATrainer.cs`) cannot produce an answer that contains characters above U+00FF. For Korean, Chinese, Japanese, Cyrillic and similar text, the predicted answer comes out with those characters missing, so exact match is unreachable whatever the model learned.

### Cause

The predicted answer is not sliced out of the context string. It is decoded from the span's token ids:

```csharp
// QATrainer.cs (main), in the mapper that fills PredictedAnswersBuffer
_parent.Tokenizer.Decode(
    _parent.Tokenizer.RobertaModel().ConvertOccurrenceRanksToIds(contextIds).ToArray()
        .AsSpan(predictStart - questionLength - 2, predictEnd - predictStart).ToArray())
```

The tokenizer comes from `TokenizerExtensions.GetInstance`, which calls `EnglishRobertaTokenizer.Create(...)` with the default `filterUnsupportedChars = true`. On that path `EnglishRobertaTokenizer.MapIdToToken` maps each token character through `UnicodeToByte` and appends the byte value as a `char`. Every output character is therefore ≤ U+00FF, and multi-byte UTF-8 sequences are never reassembled into the original characters.

### Reproduction

1. Train `mlContext.MulticlassClassification.Trainers.QuestionAnswer(...)` on a small SQuAD-format dataset whose contexts and answers are in Korean (any non-Latin script shows the same behavior).
2. Transform a test set and read the `Answer` column.

Observed with 26 training rows and 10 epochs: training completes normally, but all 8 predicted answers contain only the digits, ASCII punctuation and spaces of their spans, with every Hangul character missing, e.g. `"12  ,   1 100"`. Character-level F1 is about 0.05–0.08 and exact match is 0.

### Expected behavior

The predicted answer is the corresponding substring of the context, in whatever script the context uses.

### Suggested fix

Map the predicted token span back to character offsets in the original context (the tokenizer already provides offsets via `EncodeToTokens`) and return `context.Substring(start, length)`, instead of decoding the ids. Alternatively, decode byte-level tokens to bytes and UTF-8-decode them (`filterUnsupportedChars: false` with proper byte reassembly).

### Environment

- Microsoft.ML 5.0.0, Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp 0.23.0 (behavior also matches the current `main` source)
- .NET 10, Windows 11, CPU
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "QuestionAnsweringTrainer cannot produce answers with characters above U+00FF (answer is decoded one byte per character)" (#7749)

Issues.Title: Add PredictBatch to PredictionEngineBase for zero-allocation batch scoring (fixes #6422)
Issues.Body:
## Problem

When scoring many examples in a loop with `Predict()`, each call allocates a new `TDst` object:

```csharp
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
    results[i] = engine.Predict(examples[i]); // new TDst() on every call
```

For throughput-sensitive scenarios (real-time inference, batch pipelines), this creates constant GC pressure proportional to the number of predictions.

## Solution

Add `PredictBatch(TSrc[] examples, TDst[] predictions, int count = -1)` to `PredictionEngineBase<TSrc,TDst>`. The caller pre-allocates a `TDst[]` pool once; each element is filled in-place with no new object allocations in the hot path.

```csharp
var examples   = new InputData[N];   // filled by caller
var predictions = new OutputData[N]; // allocated once, reused forever
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) predictions[i] = new OutputData();

engine.PredictBatch(examples, predictions); // zero new() in hot path
```

## Benchmark

10,000 predictions on a `CopyColumns` pipeline:

| Approach | GC bytes allocated |
|---|---|
| `Predict()` loop | 240,000 bytes |
| `PredictBatch()` | 0 bytes |

## Changes

- `src/Microsoft.ML.Data/Prediction/PredictionEngine.cs` — new `PredictBatch` method on `PredictionEngineBase<TSrc,TDst>`
- `test/Microsoft.ML.Tests/PredictionEngineBatchTests.cs` — 4 new xUnit tests covering object reuse, correctness parity with `Predict()`, partial batch via `count`, and argument validation

Fixes #6422
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add PredictBatch to PredictionEngineBase for zero-allocation batch scoring (fixes #6422)" (#7748)

Issues.Title: Dispose TensorFlow sessions in legacy pipelines
Issues.Body:
## Summary
- make `ILegacyDataLoader` implement `IDisposable` and update legacy command and utility owners to dispose their bound pipelines deterministically
- make `LegacyCompositeDataLoader` dispose its transforms in reverse order and then its underlying loader
- explicitly dispose TensorFlow models loaded by tests and add coverage proving that disposing one transformed view does not invalidate another view sharing the same transformer
- dispose nested loaders and streams owned by `TransposeLoader` and `PartitionedFileLoader`

## Why
An undisposed TensorFlow.NET `Session` could reach finalization during process shutdown, after TensorFlow.NET had already disposed its global thread-local state. That caused an `ObjectDisposedException` from `BaseSession.DisposeUnmanagedResources` and could crash otherwise successful test runs.

Legacy command pipelines own a bound loader and their reconstructed transforms, but that ownership was not represented consistently. In particular, disposing an individual `RowToRowMapperTransform` view cannot dispose its parent transformer because modern callers may create multiple views from the same transformer. This change keeps ordinary transformed views non-owning while making `LegacyCompositeDataLoader` explicitly dispose the parent transformers that its legacy pipeline owns.

Making disposal part of the `ILegacyDataLoader` contract also exposes nested resource ownership in loaders such as `TransposeLoader` and `PartitionedFileLoader`. Their cached or per-file loaders are now retained for the required lifetime and disposed with their readers and streams. Lazy `TransposeLoader` candidates are verified before publication, and candidates that lose the initialization race are disposed.

## Validation
- full `net48` TensorFlow test suite: 37 passed, 2 skipped
- targeted transformed-view TensorFlow regression tests passed
- targeted transposer tests: 2 passed
- partitioned loader tests: 2 passed
- affected source projects build successfully

Fixes #7730
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Dispose TensorFlow sessions in legacy pipelines" (#7733)

Issues.Title: Dispose TensorFlow sessions before test process cleanup
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7730

## Summary

- Dispose the legacy view chain created by `ShowSchemaCommand`, from the final transform back to its source.
- Explicitly dispose TensorFlow models and transformers owned by TensorFlow tests.

## Why

The TensorFlow.NET `Session` finalizer can crash during test-process shutdown if it runs after TensorFlow.NET has disposed its global thread-local state. The `showschema` command constructed a TensorFlow-backed legacy pipeline but did not release its transforms when the command completed.

`ShowSchemaCommand` owns the pipeline returned by `CreateAndSaveLoader`, so it now materializes that pipeline's view chain and deterministically disposes every disposable view in downstream-to-source order.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Dispose TensorFlow sessions before test process cleanup" (#7747)

Issues.Title: Fix BPE merge parsing for carriage return tokens
Issues.Body:
Fixes #6800.

`StreamReader.ReadLine` treats a lone carriage return as a line terminator. Hugging Face Tokenizers instead splits BPE merge files on LF and removes one preceding CR for a CRLF ending. As a result, ML.NET truncated a carriage-return merge token and rejected the reported file.

This change reads the merge file as a whole, splits it on LF, and removes only the CR belonging to a CRLF line ending.

Adds synchronous and asynchronous regression coverage for the reported `; <CR><CR><LF>` byte sequence.

Validation:
- The `vocab.json` and `merges.txt` files attached to #6800 load successfully
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix BPE merge parsing for carriage return tokens" (#7746)

Issues.Title: Create higher level convenient methods for DatabaseLoader
Issues.Body:
This PR provides overrides for `DatabaseLoader.Load` and for the `DatabaseSource` constructor, to simplify API usage. The issue covers two specific scenarios where 'sugar' might be useful:

1. A "sugar method that loads directly from the arguments of DatabaseSource"
2. Provision of a `DbConnection` instead of a `DbProviderFactory`

## Summary

- Added an override for `DatabaseLoader.Load(..)` to allow inline creation of `DatabaseSource`
- Adjusted `DatabaseSource` so that it tracks whether it was provided with a `DbConnection`, or the means to create a `DbConnection`.
- Updated `DatabaseLoader.Cursor` to track whether it owns the `DbConnection` (and thus should dispose it), or whether the connection was provided, in which case the owner would have responsibility for disposing.
- Added tests to assert that the `DatabaseLoader.Load` and `DatabaseSource` constructor overrides are functionally equivalent.

## Discussion

The approach I've taken means that the `DatabaseSource` API has not changed, barring the addition of a `DbConnection` property, so this update is backwards compatible, as you'd expect. If the caller provides a `DbConnection` instead of a `DbProviderFactory` and a connection string, then the caller is responsible for opening the connection.

I considered moving the creation of the connection into `DatabaseSource`, but this presents some difficulties around how to handle `IDisposable`, so the connection is created in the `Cursor` class instead.

It could be argued that the enum added to `DatabaseSource` is superfluous, but I think it's a small amount of additional complexity which helps to clarify intent to anyone unfamiliar with the code.

## Validation

- New tests:
  - Check that overrides for `DatabaseLoader.Load` result in the same output
  - Check that overrides for `DatabaseSource` constructor result in the same output
  - Check that provision of `DbConnection` works whether the connection is already open or not
- Ran `dotnet build` in */src/Microsoft.ML.Data* 
- Ran `dotnet test` in */tests/Microsoft.ML.Tests* - 0 failed, 923 succeeded, 57 skipped

Closes #4182
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Create higher level convenient methods for DatabaseLoader" (#7741)

Issues.Title: Add ARM64 SIMD support for sparse CPU math
Issues.Body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`CpuMathUtils.DotProductSparse` and indexed `AddScale` currently use scalar loops on ARM64. Their optimized paths depend on SSE/AVX. These operations are used in sparse L-BFGS training and linear-model prediction.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Investigate ARM64 SIMD implementations for these two operations. Preserve the existing x86 paths and scalar fallback. Enable the new paths only where benchmarks show a benefit.

Validation should cover:
- Different stored-entry counts and index layouts, including short inputs and scalar tails.
- Correctness against scalar reference results, with hardware intrinsics enabled and disabled.
- L-BFGS training, model save/load, and prediction.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Retain scalar loops where SIMD does not improve performance, especially for short inputs. Dense TensorPrimitives operations are not a direct replacement for indexed sparse math.

**Additional context**
Related: #6875 migrated dense operations to TensorPrimitives but left these sparse operations unchanged.

Relevant source: [DotProductSparse](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/66201e961e367187ff23135fabeef9ac00c20f06/src/Microsoft.ML.CpuMath/CpuMathUtils.netcoreapp.cs#L397-L425) and [indexed AddScale](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/66201e961e367187ff23135fabeef9ac00c20f06/src/Microsoft.ML.CpuMath/CpuMathUtils.netcoreapp.cs#L197-L225).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Add ARM64 SIMD support for sparse CPU math" (#7740)

Issues.Title: Separate DataFrame converters into basic and dependency-specific packages
Issues.Body:
Separate existing converters from the DataFrame core so consumers only acquire the format-specific dependencies they need.

Proposed packages:

- `Microsoft.Data.Analysis`: DataFrame, columns, storage and existing data-wrangling operations. Retains `IDataView` implementation and existing ML.NET interoperability.
- `Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Converters`: Existing CSV and ADO.NET converters, using core and framework APIs without database-provider dependencies.
- `Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Arrow`: Existing Arrow conversion and the `Apache.Arrow` dependency.

Additional converters can be implemented as independent packages using the public DataFrame API, without modifying the core library. Converters requiring external libraries should have separate packages rather than introducing those dependencies into core or the basic-converters package.

Issues.Title: Add reusable inference orchestration and dynamic batching
Issues.Body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Efficiently hosting custom AI models requires more than invoking a model for one request at a time. Applications may need to collect requests into bounded time windows, create batches, route work across model instances or devices, limit concurrency, and account for available accelerator memory. Teams that cannot use a separate inference server currently have to build and operate this orchestration themselves.

This is difficult to implement reliably and can prevent applications from fully utilizing GPUs while meeting latency targets.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Investigate and provide reusable inference-orchestration building blocks for in-process .NET model hosting. The scope should consider:

- Dynamic batching with configurable maximum batch size and wait time.
- Backpressure, cancellation, queue limits, and per-request result correlation.
- Concurrency control and routing across model sessions, execution providers, or devices.
- Model placement and admission decisions informed by available memory or configured resource budgets.
- Metrics for queue time, batch composition, execution time, utilization, and rejected work.
- Extensible model-runner contracts so orchestration is not tied to a single inference backend.

A first increment could focus on a bounded dynamic-batching scheduler and leave memory-aware multi-model placement as a later extension.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Applications can build this with channels, queues, semaphores, and backend-specific session pools, or deploy a separate inference server such as NVIDIA Triton. Those approaches may be unsuitable when inference must remain in-process, model calls are interleaved with application logic, or deployment constraints prohibit an additional service.

**Additional context**
This request was identified in the “Bonus” section of the discussion that became #7383, originating in microsoft/semantic-kernel#9793. It is distinct from tokenizer batching: this issue concerns scheduling and executing inference requests after application inputs are ready for model processing.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted with AI assistance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Add reusable inference orchestration and dynamic batching" (#7737)

Issues.Title: Add high-level task inference pipelines
Issues.Body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Hugging Face task pipelines provide a high-level path from application input to model result: preprocessing and tokenization, batched model invocation, and task-specific post-processing. In .NET, users migrating custom models generally have to compose these stages themselves and understand the different tokenizer, tensor, and inference-runtime APIs involved.

This makes otherwise common inference scenarios substantially harder to implement correctly and efficiently, especially for teams migrating from Python. #7384 can document how to assemble a pipeline, but it does not track providing a reusable product abstraction.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Provide reusable, backend-aware inference pipeline abstractions for common tasks, beginning with a narrowly scoped task such as text classification. A pipeline should be able to:

- Accept single inputs and batches.
- Apply the configured tokenizer and produce the model's required inputs, including masks and token-type IDs where applicable.
- Invoke a supported model backend without unnecessary conversions or copies.
- Apply task-specific post-processing such as softmax, score selection, and label mapping.
- Expose configuration and lower-level results for callers that need to customize individual stages.
- Permit alternative tokenizer and model-runner implementations rather than coupling the abstraction to one model format.

The initial design could establish composable preprocessing, model-execution, and post-processing contracts before adding more task-specific pipelines.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Applications can implement their own pipeline for each model and task. Samples and migration documentation reduce the discovery cost, but they do not provide shared behavior, extension points, validation, or a consistent performance-oriented implementation.

**Additional context**
This request was identified while splitting the feedback in #7383, which originated in microsoft/semantic-kernel#9793. The original example was equivalent functionality to Hugging Face's `TextClassificationPipeline`, not necessarily API compatibility with that Python type.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted with AI assistance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Add high-level task inference pipelines" (#7736)

Issues.Title: [Tokenizers] Add a Hugging Face-style tokenizer factory
Issues.Body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Migrating a custom Hugging Face tokenizer to .NET requires the caller to know the tokenizer implementation, identify and load the correct vocabulary and merge files, interpret tokenizer configuration, and manually map those resources to the corresponding `Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers` type. In Python, `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)` handles this discovery and construction from a model directory or tokenizer configuration.

This gap makes migration harder and encourages application-specific loader code. #7384 can document the current process, but documentation alone does not provide an equivalent loading abstraction.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Provide a factory API that creates the appropriate tokenizer from Hugging Face tokenizer artifacts, for example from a model directory or `tokenizer.json` file. The factory should:

- Detect the supported tokenizer implementation and construct the corresponding .NET tokenizer.
- Read the relevant tokenizer configuration, vocabulary, merges, special tokens, normalizer, pre-tokenizer, post-processor, and decoder settings when supported.
- Report unsupported tokenizer types or configuration sections explicitly rather than silently changing behavior.
- Allow callers to inspect the concrete tokenizer or its capabilities when implementation-specific behavior is needed.

The final API shape does not need to match Python, but the migration experience should be comparable to `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)` for supported formats.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Callers can identify the tokenizer type themselves and write adapters around individual tokenizer constructors. A migration guide can explain those steps, but every consuming library still has to reproduce the detection, configuration mapping, validation, and error handling.

**Additional context**
This request was identified while splitting the feedback in #7383, which originated in microsoft/semantic-kernel#9793. Related format-specific gaps should remain separately trackable, while this issue covers the complete discovery-and-construction experience.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted with AI assistance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Tokenizers] Add a Hugging Face-style tokenizer factory" (#7735)

Issues.Title: Investigate removing or simplifying ML.NET's OpenMP dependency
Issues.Body:
Some ML.NET components require a separate OpenMP installation on Linux and macOS. This complicates deployment and can cause library loading failures or runtime conflicts.

Investigate whether we can remove this requirement by:
- Including compatible OpenMP runtimes in the NuGet packages.
- Building affected libraries without OpenMP.
- Replacing direct OpenMP use where practical.

MKL, Symbolic SGD, and LightGBM currently depend on OpenMP. Removing MKL alone would not remove all dependencies. Compare performance, numerical correctness, and compatibility before selecting an approach.

Related: #7061, #5569, and the [extra dependencies guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/machine-learning/how-to-guides/install-extra-dependencies).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Investigate removing or simplifying ML.NET's OpenMP dependency" (#7734)

Issues.Title: BertTokenizer: `RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true` fails to strip accents from precomposed characters under invariant globalization
Issues.Body:
`BertOptions.RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true` is the setting that makes `BertTokenizer` strip accents, as uncased BERT vocabularies expect: `café` becomes `cafe`. Accent stripping works by decomposing the text to Unicode Form D and dropping the non-spacing marks. Under globalization-invariant mode, `string.Normalize` returns its input unchanged — that is [documented behaviour](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6f4751a142ca0e879d60cb4091356bb9d346143e/docs/design/features/globalization-invariant-mode.md#string-normalization) — so there are no marks to drop. Precomposed accented characters remain intact; for vocabularies such as all-MiniLM-L6-v2, this can cause affected words to miss their expected WordPiece decomposition and become `[UNK]`.

Nothing signals this. `BertTokenizer.Create` succeeds, encoding succeeds, and for precomposed text the output is identical to having left the option off.

Invariant globalization is common in size-optimised .NET deployments. Microsoft's Alpine and Ubuntu Chiseled images ship without ICU (their [`extra` variants](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-docker/blob/7a1cdd5dd426ae782d7304ab8af476855790186a/documentation/image-variants.md) add it), and the .NET 10 Native AOT templates enable it: [`dotnet new console --aot`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/fd7d9df34dec5bf71ff2ad9869335644a33b9925/template_feed/Microsoft.DotNet.Common.ProjectTemplates.10.0/content/ConsoleApplication-CSharp/Company.ConsoleApplication1.csproj), [`dotnet new worker --aot`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0ef4bbfa3291b306a21e5001cb0491277bdd35bc/src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/Worker-CSharp.csproj.in) and [`dotnet new webapiaot`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0ef4bbfa3291b306a21e5001cb0491277bdd35bc/src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/WebApiAot-CSharp.csproj.in) all set `<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>`. A service that tokenizes correctly in development can silently stop stripping accents when deployed in one of these configurations.
### Reproduction

The reproduction below uses the `vocab.txt` from `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

```csharp
using System.Text;
using Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers;

var vocabPath = args[0];
var vocab = File.ReadAllLines(vocabPath);
var tokenizer = BertTokenizer.Create(vocabPath, new BertOptions { RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true });

Console.WriteLine($"Normalize(FormD) of \"\\u00e9\": {"\u00e9".Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormD).Length} code unit(s)");
var ids = tokenizer.EncodeToIds("Café crème brûlée in São Paulo, naïve résumé");
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(' ', ids.Select(id => vocab[id])));
```

Run it once as built, and once in invariant mode:

```
dotnet run -- path/to/vocab.txt
dotnet run -p:InvariantGlobalization=true -- path/to/vocab.txt
```

**Under ICU:**

```
Normalize(FormD) of "\u00e9": 2 code unit(s)
[CLS] cafe cr ##eme br ##ule ##e in sao paulo , naive resume [SEP]
```

**Under invariant globalization:**

```
Normalize(FormD) of "\u00e9": 1 code unit(s)
[CLS] [UNK] [UNK] [UNK] in [UNK] paulo , [UNK] [UNK] [SEP]
```

The ICU output matches Hugging Face's `BertTokenizer` exactly. The invariant output is identical to running with `RemoveNonSpacingMarks = false`.

Only precomposed input is affected; input that is already decomposed is handled correctly because its combining marks are present to be dropped.

### Expected behaviour

Either of these would remove the silent failure:

1. **Strip accents without relying on `string.Normalize`,** for example by carrying the decomposition data the option needs, so it behaves the same in every globalization mode; or
2. **Fail loudly:** throw from `BertTokenizer.Create` when `RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true` and decomposition is unavailable, with a message naming the fix (`<InvariantGlobalization>false</InvariantGlobalization>`, or an ICU-carrying image such as a chiseled `-extra` variant).

The check for (2) is one line at construction: `"\u00e9".Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormD).Length == 2`.

### Impact

In my test with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, mean pooling, and cosine similarity against the ICU tokenization, the embeddings of affected text diverge substantially:

| input | ICU | invariant |
|---|--:|--:|
| `Café crème brûlée in São Paulo, naïve résumé` | 1.000000 | 0.333027 |
| a French sentence | 1.000000 | 0.545866 |
| a Spanish sentence | 1.000000 | 0.502484 |
| a German sentence | 1.000000 | 0.572320 |
| accented capitals (`ÉCOLE ÉLÉMENTAIRE`) | 1.000000 | 0.089375 |
| plain ASCII | 1.000000 | 1.000000 |

### Versions

- Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 2.0.0 and 3.0.0-preview.26457.2, identical output
- .NET 10.0.12

### Related

#7724 and #7725 report other `BertTokenizer` differences from Hugging Face's tokenizer. This one is independent of them: the output is correct under ICU and wrong only because of the globalization mode.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "BertTokenizer: `RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true` fails to strip accents from precomposed characters under invariant globalization" (#7728)

Issues.Title: Fix Unix path handling in result-processor tests
Issues.Body:
Addresses dotnet/machinelearning#26.

Result-processor tests fail to generate `-rp.txt` files when absolute Unix input paths are interpreted as command-line options. A Windows-only guard has been masking this failure on Linux and macOS.

## Changes

- Use the supported `in=` and `o=` arguments with `CmdQuoter` to escape paths correctly.
- Check the result processor's exit code and remove the Windows-only guard.
- Add four regression cases covering multiple absolute input paths, spaces, and balanced and unmatched braces.
- Add ten missing macOS arm64 result-summary baselines. Their metrics exactly match the existing macOS training-output baselines; shared baselines and comparison tolerances are unchanged.

## Validation

- Affected predictor tests on macOS arm64 with .NET 8: 51 passed, 0 failed, 44 existing skips.
- All four new regression cases fail with the original helper and pass with the fix.
- Windows and Linux have not been tested. Removing the guard also enables Linux result-summary checks, so its baselines still need validation.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix Unix path handling in result-processor tests" (#7727)

Issues.Title: BertTokenizer silently drops symbol characters ($ + = < > | ~ ^ ` ° ©, emoji)
Issues.Body:
## Description

With default options, `BertTokenizer` deletes every character in the Unicode symbol categories (`Sm`, `Sc`, `Sk`, `So`) instead of tokenizing it. That covers the ASCII characters ``$ + < = > ^ ` | ~`` and non-ASCII ones such as `°`, `©` and emoji. Nothing is emitted, not even `[UNK]`, and nothing warns that input was lost.

Hugging Face's BERT basic tokenizer keeps all of them. It treats the ASCII symbols as punctuation — `_is_punctuation` counts every printable non-alphanumeric ASCII character — splits them into their own tokens, and passes any other character to WordPiece, which yields a vocabulary token such as `°c`, `©` or `£10`, or `[UNK]` when the character is not in the vocabulary, as with emoji.

That rule is not specific to HF. It comes from the original BERT release, whose `tokenization.py` names three of the affected characters outright:

```
# We treat all non-letter/number ASCII as punctuation.
# Characters such as "^", "$", and "`" are not in the Unicode
# Punctuation class but we treat them as punctuation anyways, for
# consistency.
```

`BertTokenizer`'s own remarks state that its implementation "is based on the original Bert implementation in the Hugging Face Transformers library".

If the current pattern is deliberate — a decision that `BertTokenizer`'s default should follow Unicode's `\p{P}` rather than BERT's own `_is_punctuation` rule — please share the reasoning, and I'll close this.

## Versions

- Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers **2.0.0** and **3.0.0-preview.26457.2**, with identical results
- .NET 10.0.12, macOS arm64
- Vocabulary: `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` `vocab.txt` (uncased BERT)
- Reference: Hugging Face `tokenizers` 0.21.1, `BertWordPieceTokenizer(vocab, lowercase=True)`
- Cosine column: `onnxruntime` 1.22.0, mean pooling over the token ids

## Reproduce

```csharp
using Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers;

var vocab = File.ReadAllLines("vocab.txt");
var tokenizer = BertTokenizer.Create("vocab.txt", new BertOptions());
foreach (var input in new[]
{
    "costs $5 + tax = $6", "a+b=c", "if (a < b && c > d) { x = y | z; }",
    "The temperature was 5 °C", "\U0001F4AF great product \U0001F44D", "\U0001F680",
})
    Console.WriteLine($"{input} -> {string.Join(' ', tokenizer.EncodeToIds(input).Select(id => vocab[id]))}");
```

## Expected vs actual

| input | actual | expected (HF `tokenizers`) | cosine ¹ |
|---|---|---|--:|
| `costs $5 + tax = $6` | `costs 5 tax 6` | `costs $ 5 + tax = $ 6` | 0.915 |
| `a+b=c` | `a b c` | `a + b = c` | **0.649** |
| `if (a < b && c > d) { x = y \| z; }` | `if ( a b & & c d ) { x y z ; }` | `if ( a < b & & c > d ) { x = y \| z ; }` | 0.912 |
| `The temperature was 5 °C` | `the temperature was 5 c` | `the temperature was 5 °c` | 0.905 |
| `💯 great product 👍` | `great product` | `[UNK] great product [UNK]` | **0.701** |
| `🚀` | *(nothing)* | `[UNK]` | — |

`[CLS]`/`[SEP]` omitted. ¹ Cosine between `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` mean-pooled embeddings of the actual and expected token ids, run through ONNX Runtime.

No built-in `BertOptions` setting preserves BERT basic-tokenization semantics while correcting this behavior. `BertOptions.PreTokenizer` can be overridden with a custom pre-tokenizer, as shown below.

## Cause

With `ApplyBasicTokenization = true` (the default), `BertTokenizer` uses `PreTokenizer.CreateWordOrPunctuation`, whose pattern is:

```
\w+|[\p{P}]
```

A symbol matches neither alternative, so the regex steps over it and it never reaches WordPiece.

## A pattern that matches HF

Splitting off Unicode punctuation plus the ASCII symbols HF counts as punctuation, and keeping every other run of non-whitespace intact, reproduces HF's tokens:

```
[\p{P}$+<=>^`|~]|[^\s\p{P}$+<=>^`|~]+
```

Passing this through `BertOptions.PreTokenizer = new RegexPreTokenizer(regex, specialTokens)` gives tokens identical to HF `tokenizers` on 18 of the 21 inputs we checked (those above, plus capitalisation, punctuation, accents with `RemoveNonSpacingMarks = true`, CJK, a 109-token paragraph and a 323-token passage). The three that still differ contain a bare `\n` or `\t`, the separate issue #7724. That option is also the workaround until the default changes.

One caveat for anyone applying it as a workaround: HF's `_clean_text` deletes format characters (`Cf`) before tokenizing, while `BertNormalizer` deletes only `Cc`. The default pattern happens to split at a zero-width space and this one does not, so against HF `"zero\u200bwidth"` moves from 0.800 to 0.250 and `"soft\u00adhyphen"` from 0.554 to 0.091. Deleting `Cf` alongside brings both to 1.000.

`BertTokenizer` is the only caller of `CreateWordOrPunctuation` in this repository, but the method is public and documents its pattern. Changing only the default that `BertTokenizer` picks may be safer than changing that method.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "BertTokenizer silently drops symbol characters ($ + = < > | ~ ^ ` ° ©, emoji)" (#7725)

Issues.Title: Update Semantic Kernel to 1.71.0 and required dependencies
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Update ten version properties in `eng/Versions.props` to address [CVE-2026-25592 / GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4):

- Semantic Kernel: `1.48.0` -> `1.71.0`, the first patched Core version listed by the advisory.
- Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions: `9.5.0` -> `10.2.0`, to meet the new dependency minimum.
- Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, DependencyInjection, DependencyInjection.Abstractions, IO.Pipelines, Numerics.Tensors, Text.Encodings.Web, Text.Json, and Threading.Channels: `9.0.4` -> `10.0.2`.

The runtime updates prevent central-version downgrade errors, including the `netstandard2.0` dependencies of Tokenizers and the internal analyzer. No C# changes, new package references, target-framework changes, or suppressions are included.

The Core alert comes from test/sample dependencies. The shipping GenAI manifests reference Abstractions; the review found no use of the affected SessionsPythonPlugin. This PR does not claim confirmed shipping exposure.

Related: #7720. The separate GenAI removal PR, #7719, is still open; this change updates the dependencies while those projects remain in `main`.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, with SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26411.119` and test runtime `8.0.31`:

- Built the GenAI sample and all four GenAI libraries for `net8.0` with the existing analyzers enabled.
- Built Tokenizers for `netstandard2.0` and the internal analyzer.
- Ran both existing Phi `SemanticKernelTests`: 2 passed, 0 failed.
- Confirmed the sample and Phi test dependency graphs resolve Core and Abstractions to `1.71.0`, and AI.Abstractions to `10.2.0`.

The version properties are shared across the repository. Full CI, the remaining x64 GenAI tests, package/consumer checks, and a fresh component scan are still needed before release.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Update Semantic Kernel to 1.71.0 and required dependencies" (#7723)

Issues.Title: Fix nightly test restore with Central Package Management
Issues.Body:
Fixes `NU1010` when restoring `Microsoft.ML.NightlyBuild.Tests` or the full solution.

The Central Package Management conversion removed the placeholder versions from the nightly package references without adding corresponding `PackageVersion` items. This caused solution restore, including restore initiated by C# Dev Kit, to fail.

## Changes

- Add placeholder `PackageVersion` items for the nightly-build dependencies.
- Add the placeholder `Microsoft.ML` package version used by `TestFrameworkDependency.props`.
- Update `Microsoft.ML.NugetPackageVersionUpdater` to rewrite `PackageVersion` items instead of `PackageReference` items.
- Preserve the nightly pipeline behaviour, where placeholder versions are replaced with the latest nightly package versions.

## Validation

- Restored `Microsoft.ML.NightlyBuild.Tests` with `ReferenceTypeForTestFramework=NuGet`.
- Restored the full `Microsoft.ML.sln`.
- Built `Microsoft.ML.NugetPackageVersionUpdater`.
- Verified that the updater replaces versions in both dependency props files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix nightly test restore with Central Package Management" (#7721)

Issues.Title: Remove Microsoft.ML.GenAI.* packages and their supporting code
Issues.Body:
The Microsoft.ML.GenAI.* packages introduce model-specific implementations, integrations and dependencies that require maintenance alongside the rest of ML.NET.
Removing these packages would reduce the maintenance and dependency surface while preserving the independently useful TorchSharp trainers and tokenizer packages.

Remove the following packages from the repository:

Microsoft.ML.GenAI.Core
Microsoft.ML.GenAI.LLaMA
Microsoft.ML.GenAI.Mistral
Microsoft.ML.GenAI.Phi
Include everything used exclusively to support them:

Associated test projects, approval baselines, model configurations and samples.
Solution entries and any GenAI-specific build or packaging configuration.
GenAI-only NuGet dependencies and unused version properties.
Dedicated design documentation and obsolete third-party notices.
References in current documentation, dependency diagrams and repository tooling guidance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Remove Microsoft.ML.GenAI.* packages and their supporting code" (#7720)
